subject: discover aspect ratio from inside a stat function?

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: discover aspect ratio from inside a stat function?
parts:
I'm (foolishly) trying to write a stat that will draw a smooth path that encloses a specified set of x,y points (if anyone already has a solution for this please let me know!!).  One of my current problems is that for some of the computations I want to do, it would be extremely useful to know the aspect ratio of the plot -- this would be similar to the problem of drawing a circle on a plot regardless of the x/y values, as in

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/6862742/draw-a-circle-with-ggplot2

I'm afraid, though, that beyond the narrow technical difficulty of "how do I recover this information within the scope of a stat?", this may be harder -- because the aspect ratio may not even be defined at the time the stat is computed.  I might be better off trying to construct my path as a grob and use annotation_custom to add it <http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/annotation_custom.html>, but I'd ideally like to be able to enclose/annotate *different* sets of points in different facets ...

My current, not entirely workable strategy for what I'm calling StatEncircle is:

   - find convex-hull of points to be encircled
   - expand convex hull by pushing points away from the centroid (this is where I need the aspect ratio)
   - use graphics::xspline to construct a smooth curve through the points (this part also needs work ...)

Any input is welcome.

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: discover aspect ratio from inside a stat function?
parts:
OK, next stupid question.

The code below works fine with a dummy (unused) new default aesthetic called 'xx' and set to a value of 2. If I make the minimal change of setting the default value for xx to "a", or many other things (other strings, 0, positive integers, positive floats), it works.  If I set it to -1 or (my current working hypothesis) *any other value that requires any evaluation/parsing by R* (-1 requires evaluation because it is really (unary minus(1))), I get

Error in rep(value[[k]], length.out = n) :
  attempt to replicate an object of type 'language'

I'm guessing (again, just my current working hypothesis) that there is some kind of magic lazy stuff going on in the guts of ggproto/ggplot that stops this from working.

Am I being an idiot?
Does this constitute a bug or just an infelicity?
Any thoughts for a workaround (a really, really ugly case that I just thought of, since I need the shape parameter to be able to vary from -1 to 1, is to pass the shape as a value on [0,2] and then subtract 1 once I get inside the function ...)


=========
library("ggplot2")
library("grid")

g0 <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point()
.

GeomXSpline <- ggproto("GeomXSpline", Geom,
  required_aes = c("x", "y"),
  default_aes = aes(colour = "black", xx=2),
  draw_key = draw_key_point,

  draw_panel = function(data, panel_scales, coord) {
    coords <- coord$transform(data, panel_scales)
    print(head(coords))
    grid::xsplineGrob(
      coords$x, coords$y,
      gp = grid::gpar(col = coords$colour)
    )
  }
)

geom_xspline <- function(mapping = NULL, data = NULL, stat = "identity",
                         position = "identity", na.rm = FALSE, show.legend = NA,                               inherit.aes = TRUE, ...) {
  layer(
    geom = GeomXSpline, mapping = mapping,  data = data, stat = stat,
    position = position, show.legend = show.legend, inherit.aes = inherit.aes,
    params = list(na.rm = na.rm, ...)
  )
}

g0 + geom_xspline(colour="red")

  •   is there a way to tell ggplot2 that the geom has generated grobs that cover a wider range in x-y space than the original points passed to it, i.e. to expand the panel so that it includes the full generated grob?
  • it feels like these geoms might be useful, but not really worth rolling out a whole separate package. Is there a  community-developed 'ggplotrix' or 'ggmisc' package taking general contributions?  I might contact the maintainer of https://cran.rstudio.com/web/packages/ggpmisc/ ...



On Wednesday, March 2, 2016 at 3:25:30 PM UTC-5, Ben Bolker wrote:
OK, next stupid question.

The code below works fine with a dummy (unused) new default aesthetic called 'xx' and set to a value of 2. If I make the minimal change of setting the default value for xx to "a", or many other things (other strings, 0, positive integers, positive floats), it works.  If I set it to -1 or (my current working hypothesis) *any other value that requires any evaluation/parsing by R* (-1 requires evaluation because it is really (unary minus(1))), I get

Error in rep(value[[k]], length.out = n) :
  attempt to replicate an object of type 'language'

I'm guessing (again, just my current working hypothesis) that there is some kind of magic lazy stuff going on in the guts of ggproto/ggplot that stops this from working.

Am I being an idiot?
Does this constitute a bug or just an infelicity?
Any thoughts for a workaround (a really, really ugly case that I just thought of, since I need the shape parameter to be able to vary from -1 to 1, is to pass the shape as a value on [0,2] and then subtract 1 once I get inside the function ...)


=========
library("ggplot2")
library("grid")

g0 <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) +
  geom_point()
.

GeomXSpline <- ggproto("GeomXSpline", Geom,
  required_aes = c("x", "y"),
  default_aes = aes(colour = "black", xx=2),
  draw_key = draw_key_point,

  draw_panel = function(data, panel_scales, coord) {
    coords <- coord$transform(data, panel_scales)
    print(head(coords))
    grid::xsplineGrob(
      coords$x, coords$y,
      gp = grid::gpar(col = coords$colour)
    )
  }
)

geom_xspline <- function(mapping = NULL, data = NULL, stat = "identity",
                         position = "identity", na.rm = FALSE, show.legend = NA,                               inherit.aes = TRUE, ...) {
  layer(
    geom = GeomXSpline, mapping = mapping,  data = data, stat = stat,
    position = position, show.legend = show.legend, inherit.aes = inherit.aes,
    params = list(na.rm = na.rm, ...)
  )
}

g0 + geom_xspline(colour="red")

messages.subject: Re: discover aspect ratio from inside a stat function?
parts:
I haven't looked at it, but I assume the geom_xspline is the same
(mine just wraps grid::xsplineGrob). The fun thing in my code is not
geom_xspline, but geom_encircle, which uses a combination of a convex
hull, inflation away from the centroid, and a spline interpolation to
create a smooth path around a specified set of points.
